boundaries.note: Coverage judgments are candidate interpretations of documented obligations, not approval of any proposed rule. Applicability requires an actual source baseline and inspection.

existing_rule_review.reason: Rust implementation-language discipline; overlaps approved architecture choices.
Reader-focused README separate from detailed docs and changelog.
Previous/current/delta reporting; not needed unless per-round percent bars are used.

candidates.heading: Freeze the upstream runtime and supported behavior baseline
candidates.atomic_proposal: For an authorized strict port, identify the exact upstream revision, Python interpreter/version/build and target environment before claiming behavioral equivalence.
candidates.applicability_note: General strict-port study candidate, not active until separately adopted.

candidates.heading: Track every in-scope upstream capability
candidates.atomic_proposal: For each agreed upstream capability, record its Rust implementation or replacement, independent verification status and any missing or incompatible behavior.
candidates.applicability_note: General strict-port study candidate, not active until separately adopted.

candidates.heading: Compare upstream and Rust observable results
candidates.atomic_proposal: For each reproducible in-scope case, run both implementations under equivalent inputs and relevant environment, compare outputs, exit status and side effects, and report untestable cases.
candidates.applicability_note: General strict-port study candidate, not active until separately adopted.

candidates.heading: Register and approve deviations from upstream
candidates.atomic_proposal: Record each intentional behavior deviation, supporting authorization, affected consumers, and regression cases; do not count unresolved discrepancies as compatibility.
candidates.applicability_note: General strict-port study candidate, not active until separately adopted.

candidates.heading: Establish executable replacement acceptance
candidates.atomic_proposal: Before accepting strict-port completion, require evidence of in-scope feature coverage, downstream integration and deployment behavior, with explicit unverified gaps.
candidates.applicability_note: General strict-port study candidate, not active until separately adopted.

candidates.heading: Contain and test necessary unsafe and cross-language interfaces
candidates.atomic_proposal: Where a Rust port retains unsafe or foreign-function boundaries, isolate them, document safety and ABI assumptions, and verify exposed behavior.
candidates.applicability_note: General strict-port study candidate, not active until separately adopted.

candidates.heading: Verify distribution and installation cutover
candidates.atomic_proposal: When replacing an installed upstream program, verify launch commands, runtime dependencies, installation/upgrading and return to a known-good state where recovery is required.
candidates.applicability_note: General strict-port study candidate, not active until separately adopted.

candidates.heading: Object identity, aliasing and mutation
candidates.atomic_proposal: Where externally observable, preserve Python identity-versus-equality, shared-reference mutation and copy behavior in Rust.
candidates.applicability_note: Requires confirmation that this feature or behavior is in the agreed upstream replacement contract.

candidates.heading: Dynamic typing and reflection
candidates.atomic_proposal: When used by supported consumers, preserve dynamic attribute access, callable signatures, reflection or runtime dispatch behavior.
candidates.applicability_note: Requires confirmation that this feature or behavior is in the agreed upstream replacement contract.

candidates.heading: Truthiness and implicit conversion
candidates.atomic_proposal: For each in-scope branch or interface using Python truth testing or conversion, compare behavior for relevant false-like, empty, custom and mixed-type values.
candidates.applicability_note: Requires confirmation that this feature or behavior is in the agreed upstream replacement contract.

candidates.heading: Numeric range, precision and rounding
candidates.atomic_proposal: Where numerical behavior matters, test integer range, division, float special values, decimal contexts, rounding and overflow against the source baseline.
candidates.applicability_note: Requires confirmation that this feature or behavior is in the agreed upstream replacement contract.

candidates.heading: Unicode, text and bytes semantics
candidates.atomic_proposal: For in-scope text boundaries, verify encoding/decoding, Unicode operations, normalization when expected, byte handling and error policy.
candidates.applicability_note: Requires confirmation that this feature or behavior is in the agreed upstream replacement contract.

candidates.heading: Equality, hashing and collection behavior
candidates.atomic_proposal: For exposed data structures, verify Python equality, key hashing, insertion order where guaranteed, and iteration-dependent behavior.
candidates.applicability_note: Requires confirmation that this feature or behavior is in the agreed upstream replacement contract.

candidates.heading: Exception, failure and cleanup contracts
candidates.atomic_proposal: Where observable, preserve error categories, messages when contractual, exit behavior, exception propagation and cleanup side effects.
candidates.applicability_note: Requires confirmation that this feature or behavior is in the agreed upstream replacement contract.

candidates.heading: Iterator and generator protocols
candidates.atomic_proposal: For consumed iterators/generators, verify laziness, yielded sequence, termination, exception propagation and finalization behavior.
candidates.applicability_note: Requires confirmation that this feature or behavior is in the agreed upstream replacement contract.

candidates.heading: Context manager and resource lifetime behavior
candidates.atomic_proposal: For code using with/async-with or equivalent contracts, verify acquisition, release, exception handling and early-exit behavior.
candidates.applicability_note: Requires confirmation that this feature or behavior is in the agreed upstream replacement contract.

candidates.heading: Imports, modules and dynamic discovery
candidates.atomic_proposal: When modules or dynamic imports are consumed externally, preserve agreed import names, loading/discovery behavior and failure contracts.
candidates.applicability_note: Requires confirmation that this feature or behavior is in the agreed upstream replacement contract.

candidates.heading: Installed commands, package entry points and plugins
candidates.atomic_proposal: Where the Python distribution exposes console entry points or plugins, verify that Rust replacement preserves agreed discovery and invocation interfaces.
candidates.applicability_note: Requires confirmation that this feature or behavior is in the agreed upstream replacement contract.

candidates.heading: Async task lifecycle and cancellation
candidates.atomic_proposal: For asyncio-dependent behavior, compare task ordering where observable, cancellation, timeouts, cleanup and backpressure under representative load.
candidates.applicability_note: Requires confirmation that this feature or behavior is in the agreed upstream replacement contract.

candidates.heading: Threads, processes and synchronization
candidates.atomic_proposal: For concurrency-dependent behavior, verify ordering guarantees, shared state, race freedom, process isolation and relevant interpreter-build assumptions.
candidates.applicability_note: Requires confirmation that this feature or behavior is in the agreed upstream replacement contract.

candidates.heading: Python API and extension compatibility
candidates.atomic_proposal: Where Python callers or compiled extensions must continue to work, exercise the public binding/extension interface with an independent consumer.
candidates.applicability_note: Requires confirmation that this feature or behavior is in the agreed upstream replacement contract.

candidates.heading: Serialization compatibility beyond round-trip preservation
candidates.atomic_proposal: Where a Python-produced interchange format is consumed externally, compare field types, ordering when contractual, null/missing distinctions and canonical bytes if required.
candidates.applicability_note: Requires confirmation that this feature or behavior is in the agreed upstream replacement contract.

candidates.heading: Filesystem, environment and subprocess boundaries
candidates.atomic_proposal: When upstream behavior invokes subprocesses or interacts with OS paths and environment, verify argument parsing, standard streams, exit codes, paths and permissions.
candidates.applicability_note: Requires confirmation that this feature or behavior is in the agreed upstream replacement contract.

candidates.heading: Regression corpus for Python edge behavior
candidates.atomic_proposal: For each relevant Python-specific semantic boundary, maintain representative baseline cases including error paths and counterexamples, tied to source behavior evidence.
candidates.applicability_note: Requires confirmation that this feature or behavior is in the agreed upstream replacement contract.

candidates.heading: Persisted state and legacy migration compatibility
candidates.atomic_proposal: Where the replacement reads or upgrades Python-era data/configuration, verify historical input compatibility and migration/recovery outcomes against accepted baselines.
candidates.applicability_note: Requires confirmation that this feature or behavior is in the agreed upstream replacement contract.

other_profiles.rationale: Re-apply the same method independently; normal Rust projects, Tarium projects and maintained forks have different baseline and scope conditions.

atomicity_review.criteria: A proposed normative atom expresses one independently actionable, evidence-checkable contract with an explicit context. Examples within one contract do not automatically make it composite; distinct triggers, consumers and approvals normally do.

dispositions.single_candidate: Focused enough for a later rule specimen review; not a published or approved rule.
dispositions.decompose: Original item spans separable contracts or overlaps another candidate; suggested parts require later semantic normalization and duplicate review.
dispositions.reuse_existing: No distinct new atom established by this audit; rely on existing published obligations under their conditions.

entries.rationale: NOM-0074 assumes a defined baseline but does not prescribe an auditable baseline record. Python interpreter specificity is misplaced in a language-neutral proposal.
normalized_parts: Record the authoritative upstream revision and supported comparison environment for a strict port.
For Python source ports, identify interpreter version/build and relevant implementation features in the accepted source baseline.

entries.rationale: NOM-0075 is an acceptance goal, not per-feature coverage accounting. NOM-0113 is a direct C-only analogue; avoid publishing a duplicate scoped C rule.
normalized_parts: For each in-scope upstream capability, maintain its Rust replacement mapping and independently verified status, explicitly accounting for gaps.

entries.rationale: NOM-0029 covers bug regression, not running an upstream oracle; NOM-0111 supplies the C-only precedent.
normalized_parts: Compare equivalent upstream and Rust observations for each reproducible in-scope behavior and record unresolved or unavailable comparisons.

entries.rationale: NOM-0064 already requires deviations to be recorded, but an agreed deviation decision and its effect on parity claims are different checks.
normalized_parts: Link each intentional divergence to an explicit approval and affected consumer contract.
Classify unresolved divergences as unverified or incompatible rather than verified parity.

entries.rationale: The proposed readiness test combines NOM-0075 replacement-capability MVP, NOM-0090 validation, NOM-0093 consumer testing where applicable, and NOM-0098 accepted limitations. A new duplicate umbrella gate is not justified by this audit.
Necessary unsafe/FFI boundary assurance is a coherent conditional concern, directly analogous to C-only NOM-0112. Previous citations to NOM-0033 and NOM-0041 are not substantive FFI-safety coverage.
normalized_parts: For each necessary unsafe or FFI boundary, establish and verify its safety, lifetime and ABI contract, isolating the boundary where feasible.

entries.rationale: Installation/invocation compatibility and recovery after replacement have independent applicability; general CI workflow rules are not evidence of safe cutover.
normalized_parts: Verify supported installation, runtime dependency and launch/invocation behavior when replacing a deployed upstream distribution.
When deployment replaces existing state, verify authorized upgrade, recovery and rollback procedures against representative state.

entries.rationale: Python reference identity and alias-visible mutation form one coherent externally observable object-reference contract. Do not require preserving nonobservable internals.
normalized_parts: Verify agreed identity and alias-visible mutation behavior for Python objects crossing supported interfaces.

entries.rationale: Dynamic attributes/reflection and callable signature/dispatch are separately observable contracts and need not both occur in a source project.
normalized_parts: Verify externally consumed Python attribute, reflection and dynamic type behavior.
Verify callable signature and invocation/dispatch compatibility at supported Python-facing boundaries.

entries.rationale: Truth-testing and implicit conversion are independent Python protocols with different trigger conditions and test cases.
normalized_parts: Verify Python truth-testing outcomes at in-scope decision boundaries.
Verify Python implicit and explicit conversion outcomes at in-scope interfaces.

entries.rationale: Arbitrary-precision integer, binary floating-point and decimal-context semantics can fail independently; one blanket numeric rule obscures target contracts.
normalized_parts: Verify integer range, division and overflow-equivalent behavior where source integer semantics are exposed.
Verify floating-point special values, comparison and rounding where externally consequential.
Verify Decimal precision, context and rounding where the upstream uses decimal arithmetic.

entries.rationale: Unicode/text operations and encoding/decoding of byte streams have different observables. Normalization is conditional; Python does not universally normalize strings.
normalized_parts: Verify in-scope Unicode string operations and code-point semantics.
Verify byte/text encoding, decoding and error-policy behavior at exposed interfaces.

entries.rationale: Equality/hash compatibility and collection order/iteration guarantees are distinguishable contracts. Do not imply all sets or mappings have the same ordering guarantees.
normalized_parts: Verify in-scope equality, hashing and lookup-key behavior.
Verify exposed collection iteration and ordering guarantees supported by the agreed upstream baseline.

entries.rationale: Error categories/propagation and resource cleanup are separate. Cleanup belongs to context/resource behavior under PY-09, avoiding duplicate obligations.
normalized_parts: Verify externally observable exception categories, propagation, failure returns and contractually exposed messages.
Assign cleanup-on-failure verification to PY-09 rather than duplicating a second independent cleanup rule here.

entries.rationale: Generator and iterator protocol fidelity can be expressed as one focused conditional protocol check. Resource cleanup is covered by PY-09.
normalized_parts: Verify in-scope iterator/generator lazy yield, termination and exception propagation behavior.

entries.rationale: Resource acquisition/release and exceptional exit form one context-manager lifecycle contract, including exception-suppression behavior when externally observable.
normalized_parts: Verify in-scope Python context-management resource lifecycle and exceptional-exit behavior.

entries.rationale: Python module import resolution and independently discovered plugins are distinct. Consolidate plugin discovery with PY-11 rather than generating two similar rules.
normalized_parts: Verify import/module name resolution and failure behavior where consumers rely on Python imports.
Move plugin discovery compatibility into PY-11 for de-duplication.

entries.rationale: Installed console/script entry points and third-party plugin discovery are separately consumed contracts. The plugin concern is shared with PY-10 and should be represented once.
normalized_parts: Verify distribution entry points, script commands and invocation contracts.
Verify declared plugin registration, discovery and loading contracts where supported.

entries.rationale: Cancellation/timeouts and observable task ordering/backpressure are independently testable async contracts; implementation scheduler identity need not match.
normalized_parts: Verify in-scope asynchronous cancellation, timeout and failure-cleanup behavior.
Verify promised task ordering, concurrency-limit and backpressure outcomes under representative load.

entries.rationale: Shared-memory concurrency and cross-process coordination have different contracts. GIL behavior must be tied to a documented interpreter build, not assumed globally.
normalized_parts: Verify in-scope shared-state synchronization, visibility and race-sensitive behavior.
Verify interprocess communication, isolation and process lifecycle where the Python baseline uses processes.

entries.rationale: Python-level calling contract and compiled extension/ABI compatibility have separate consumers. Neither is required if no Python-facing API is promised.
normalized_parts: Verify supported Python-callable interface behavior using an independent consumer.
Verify binary extension/embedding ABI and lifetime invariants only where compiled interoperation is part of the accepted baseline.

entries.rationale: NOM-0053 tests data round trips but not external wire-format agreement. One serialized interchange contract can cover documented bytes/types/field shapes conditional on downstream consumers.
normalized_parts: Verify externally consumed serialized representations against the source contract, including exact bytes only when those bytes are contractual.

entries.rationale: Filesystem/environment conventions and child-process interaction are independently observable. The general feature-target rule NOM-0033 is not a replacement for OS parity.
normalized_parts: Verify in-scope filesystem, path, permission and environment-variable contracts.
Verify subprocess arguments, streams, status codes and lifecycle contracts where invoked.

entries.rationale: NOM-0027/0029/0030/0032 already cover unit, regression, edge-case and deterministic tests. Source-oracle comparison is PORT-03; a duplicate Python regression-corpus rule would not add an independent norm.
Legacy data-read compatibility and upgrading persisted state are separate. General non-destructive and round-trip rules support them but do not establish a Python-era migration contract.
normalized_parts: Verify accepted historical Python-era persisted files/configurations are read compatibly.
Where migration occurs, verify transformation and available recovery/rollback against representative retained state.
